Use this pattern only when full-width and full-height separator lines partition the input into equal tiles and the output dimensions match that tile layout. Map each tile to one output cell, then infer from demonstrations which in-tile feature or count determines its value; do not assume every unusual cell or a single marker is positive.

For the demonstrated pattern with color-8 separators and 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, emit 1 when a tile contains at least two 2s, and 3 otherwise. Verify the inferred rule against all demonstrated tiles before submitting.

With zero-based coordinates, index stripe phase by `column−row` for down-right lines and `row+column` for down-left lines; verify the sign against demonstrated output.

Infer the smallest plausible period by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue. Use output examples to establish the complete phase-to-color mapping; marker positions alone may not reveal every residue. # Edge continuation

Compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and which cells are missing. The continuation may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only confirmed missing cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells.

Check each candidate against all demonstrated changed and unchanged cells. Use that evidence to select repeated copies—not rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
